title: Approve a Run With Holds Outstanding
scenario: It is 2:30 PM. The batch has one clean invoice and four are held in exceptions. The AP Manager still approves the run - but a good approval also acknowledges what is being left behind. Learn what the Manager confirms when the day is messy, not clean.
input: Payment Batch: 1 invoice (INV-59001), total 1200.00, 4 held, cutoff 3:00 PM. The AP Manager reviews the control totals and the held count, approves the run of one at 2:30 PM, and acknowledges that four invoices are held and carried forward. Approval confirms the batch is complete for what is payable and that the holds are known, not lost.
instructions: Read run approval as the human control point before funds move.
Understand that the Manager approves the payable invoice and acknowledges the four holds.
Answer the questions and validate to mint the run-approval record.

questions.prompt: The batch has 1 payable invoice and 4 held. What does the AP Manager approve?

options.text: All five invoices, to clear the queue
The run of one payable invoice, while acknowledging the four holds
Nothing until every exception is resolved

questions.explain: The run pays only what is clean - INV-59001. The Manager approves that one and acknowledges the four held invoices so they are known and carried forward, not quietly dropped.

questions.prompt: What control figures does the Manager check before approving?

options.text: The invoice count, batch total, and held count
The color of each invoice PDF

questions.explain: Count (1), total (1200), and held (4) are the control figures. They confirm the batch is complete for what is payable and that the holds are visible - the line-level checks already ran upstream.

questions.prompt: Why approve a run of one instead of waiting for the four holds to clear?

options.text: Because the clean invoice should not be delayed by unrelated exceptions
Because the cutoff does not apply to small runs

questions.explain: A clean invoice earns timely payment. Holding INV-59001 hostage to four unrelated problems would penalize a good vendor - the exceptions are worked on their own track and carried forward.

questions.prompt: What happens to the four held invoices after this approval?

options.text: They are deleted from the system
They are carried forward to be resolved and considered for a later run

questions.explain: Acknowledging the holds means they persist. The four carry forward to their owners; once resolved they can join a future batch. Approval records that they were known, not lost.

artifactOnPass.note: run of one approved; four holds carried forward

copilotPrompt: Confirm the AP Manager approves a run of one clean invoice while acknowledging four holds. Explain the control figures checked (count, total, held), why a clean invoice should not wait for unrelated exceptions, and that the holds carry forward.
successMessage: Run approved. One invoice released, four holds acknowledged and carried forward - all on the record.

intro.heading: Approving a messy day: pay the clean, acknowledge the rest

sections.title: Approval still gates the money
sections.body: Even with only one payable invoice, releasing funds is the moment that stays human. The AP Manager - not the Clerk who processed the batch - puts their name on the run before anything moves.

sections.title: A good approval acknowledges the holds
sections.body: Approving a run of one is not ignoring the four exceptions. The Manager checks the held count and acknowledges it, so the holds are visible on the record and carried forward to their owners.

sections.title: Clean work should not wait for messy work
sections.body: INV-59001 passed every check; making it wait for four unrelated problems would punish a good vendor. The exceptions run on their own track - approval lets the clean payment proceed on time.

takeaway.heading: Run approved with holds acknowledged
points: The AP Manager approved the run of one payable invoice - the human control point stays even on a messy day.
The control figures checked were count (1), total (1200), and held (4).
The four holds were acknowledged and carried forward, not dropped - visible on the record.
The clean invoice was released on time rather than waiting for four unrelated exceptions.
The workflow can now authorize a partial run while keeping outstanding holds accountable.
